diagrams.title: **Why protocols exist
diagrams.caption: **Why protocols exist.** Without a standard, every agent needs custom code for every tool, and the count explodes as you grow. With one, each side is built once and works with everything else that speaks it.

diagrams.title: **Host, clients, servers, data
diagrams.caption: **Host, clients, servers, data.** The host owns the AI and the clients; each server is a separate small program that wraps one system. Add a new system by adding a server, without touching the agent's code.

diagrams.caption: **The MCP workflow.** Use the stepper below to light up one step at a time. Notice the host never talks to a database directly: it only ever speaks MCP to servers.

diagrams.title: **One orchestrator, many independent agents
diagrams.caption: **One orchestrator, many independent agents.** The travel agent doesn't handle the details itself, and doesn't need to know how any of these agents work inside. It only needs them to speak A2A.

diagrams.title: **Client and remote agents
diagrams.caption: **Client and remote agents.** The client agent works for the user and delegates. Remote agents publish an *agent card* describing what they can do, so the client knows whom to ask.

diagrams.title: **Down to tools, across to peers
diagrams.caption: **Down to tools, across to peers.** MCP goes "down" from an agent to the tools it uses. A2A goes "across" between agents. A remote agent can use MCP for its own tools, and you never see that from outside.
